notes: PSA 15 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.25. Prostate volume 60 mL. csPCa 0.74.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management following persistent PSA elevation and prior biopsy findings.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired butcher with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed on prior biopsy. He has comorbidities including type 2 diabetes, hypercholesterolaemia, COPD, and chronic kidney disease. He is currently managed with metformin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, and salbutamol PRN. He lives alone, though his adult son is his primary contact. He reports limited mobility, using a frame and engaging only in chair-based exercises. He consumes approximately 4 units of alcohol weekly and is an ex-smoker (33 pack-years, quit in 2015). His IPSS score is 17/35, indicating moderate LUTS. He had a stable cardiology review in autumn 2024.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable with no nodularity or asymmetry, consistent with cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vitals. No lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses are noted.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
